title: Lung adenocarcinoma tumours and matched normal lung
subtitle: 101 patients · tumour and adjacent normal tissue · RNA, proteins and phosphosites

pairing.label: Patient
pairing.note: Each patient contributes one tumour and one normal-adjacent sample.

views.name: Transcriptome
views.note: Protein-coding genes; expressed (median ≥ 4, detected in ≥ 90% of samples).

views.name: Proteome
views.note: Gene-level protein abundance; missing values are not imputed.

views.name: Phosphoproteome
views.note: Single phosphosites, not normalised to protein abundance.

papers.cite: Li Y, Dou Y, et al. Proteogenomic data and resources for pan-cancer analysis. Cancer Cell 41, 1397–1406 (2023).
Gillette MA, Satpathy S, Cao S, et al. Proteogenomic characterization reveals therapeutic vulnerabilities in lung adenocarcinoma. Cell 182, 200–225 (2020).

files.name: CPTAC pan-cancer harmonized data freeze v1.2 (LUAD)

processing: Kept the 101 patients with a tumour and a normal-adjacent sample in all three layers (202 samples).
Mapped Ensembl gene IDs to HGNC symbols with org.Hs.eg.db; duplicated symbols keep the most abundant row. Phosphosites are labelled 'SYMBOL site'.
Teaching pools are label-free: features with ≤ 50% missing values (RNA: expressed genes), ranked by variance across all samples; the top 1500 per layer are shipped.
RNA–protein concordance was computed offline on all 11299 genes measured in both layers (Spearman, ≥ 20 paired observations).
Values are rounded to three decimals. No imputation is applied before shipping.
limitations: Normal-adjacent tissue is not healthy lung: it can carry field effects of the tumour and of smoking.
Tumour purity and immune/stromal content vary between patients and drive part of the variation.
Phosphosite abundance partly reflects protein abundance; the shipped values are not protein-normalised.
Genotype labels (EGFR, KRAS, TP53, STK11) and stage describe the tumour and are shown as 'Normal tissue' for normal samples.
